However, the policy must then pick out the relevant target from a long and redundant history, leading to spurious correlations and unreliable decisions as the memory load grows. Additionally, the initial noise carries no information about what the robot has seen, leaving generation without guidance toward the remembered target. To address these issues, we propose RecallFlow, a flow-policy framework that builds the source distribution from episodic memory. Recall-Relocalization relates the memory to the current view through a few recall slots, so that the source reflects where the remembered targets are now. Recall Anchors then turns each slot into a Gaussian component of the source, enabling generation to start close to the intended action instead of from noise. The transport network then completes the action from the current observation alone, keeping inference nearly as cheap as a memoryless policy. We further build a suite of memory-dependent tasks grouped by memory load and compare all policies under a matched protocol. Extensive experiments show that RecallFlow achieves a state-of-the-art average success rate of 80.4% on the public MIKASA-Robo memory benchmark, and outperforms the strongest baseline by 20.3 points on our suite and by 18.8 points on four real-robot tasks.

title: Drift-Aware Adaptive Semantic Codec Update Strategy for Dynamic Semantic Communications
authors: Bizhu Wang, Manqi Li, Shujun Han, Mengying Sun, Xiaodong Xu
publish: arXiv
abstract: Semantic communication reduces transmission overhead by conveying task-relevant semantic features, but its performance depends on the consistency between training and target-domain data distributions. In dynamic environments, distribution drift can make offline-trained semantic codec models stale and degrade transmission performance. Frequent updates alleviate this degradation but increase communication, computation, and queueing costs, whereas infrequent updates delay model adaptation. To address this tradeoff, we propose a drift-aware adaptive update strategy for dynamic semantic communication systems. Drift intensity is quantified in the semantic feature space, and Drift-Aware Age of Model (DA-AoM) is introduced to jointly capture drift-induced performance degradation, drift-dependent update service delay, and conventional update latency. Closed-form average DA-AoM expressions are derived for edge-layer M/M/1 and cloud-layer D/M/1 update scenarios, based on which the update frequency is optimized under the queueing-stability constraint. Simulations show that DA-AoM captures the joint effects of drift intensity, computing rate, bandwidth, and update frequency on model freshness beyond conventional Age of Information (AoI). The proposed strategy reduces average DA-AoM by 9.2\%--42.4\% compared with representative baselines under the same resource constraints.

title: Do 3D Point Representations Encode Architectural Functions? Probing Supervised and Pretrained Models on Urban Facades
authors: Abdiaziz Muse, Jiju Poovvancheri
publish: arXiv
abstract: Semantic labels say what a building element is, not what it does: two identical-looking windows on one facade may be operable or fixed, a column may carry load or only decorate. We ask whether 3D point representations encode such architectural function. On 22 mobile-LiDAR buildings with 15 functional attributes per element, we hold out entire buildings and compare hand-crafted descriptors, networks trained from scratch and frozen self-supervised point transformers. Descriptors and frozen features are read by the same linear layer. No network trained from scratch, from PointNet to a 108M-parameter PTv3, clearly exceeds the descriptors (0.610 mAP on functionally ambiguous elements), whereas frozen Utonia reaches 0.732. Random-weight controls of the same architectures (0.649 and 0.652) attribute the gain to pretraining (Utonia: +0.080, 95% building interval [+0.035, +0.124]). Pretrained features improve at every tested number of labelled buildings while descriptors and random features plateau, and, in the configurations we tested, fine-tuning erodes the benefit: at today's data scale, function is better read from pretrained representations than learned from scratch.

title: Improving While Deployed: Learning Proactive End-to-End Driving from Imperfect Human Takeover Data
authors: Yangang Ren, Di Zeng, Jun Li, Zirui Li, Chengjiang Zhang, Xiaoqing Ye, Ji Tao, Chen Lv
publish: arXiv
abstract: Once deployed on vehicles, end-to-end driving models continuously encounter challenging scenarios, generating valuable human takeover data that capture both model outputs and human behaviors. However, human interventions are often imperfect, as drivers may intervene too late or unnecessarily. Consequently, direct imitation can reinforce late responses or discourage otherwise appropriate maneuvers. To address this challenge, we propose an offline post-training framework that transforms imperfect takeover data into proactive supervision. We first construct diverse trajectory candidates by augmenting the plans of the deployed model and shifting recorded human corrective maneuvers earlier in time. We then train a scene-conditioned trajectory scorer to rank these candidates using expert demonstrations and unpaired preference signals from takeover logs. Using this scorer, we selectively replace pre-takeover training targets with higher-scoring candidates while retaining the original targets in normal driving scenarios. Finally, we distill the resulting targets into the driving model without changing its inference architecture. In closed-loop evaluations using real-world scenarios reconstructed with 4D Gaussian splatting, our method achieves the highest overall success rate, outperforming the deployed model, direct imitation learning and trajectory post-optimization. These results highlight a practical path toward efficient updates of deployed driving models using existing fleet logs.

title: CoScan: Multi-Scale Content-Adaptive Space-Filling Scans for Causal State-Space Image Restoration
authors: Wei Dong, Terry Ji, Yan Min, Shahram Shirani, Jun Chen, Han Zhou
publish: arXiv
abstract: Selective state-space models (SSMs) have recently shown strong potential for efficient image restoration. A central difficulty, however, is that a 2D feature map typically needs to be linearized into a 1D token sequence for causal state-space updates, making restoration performance highly sensitive to the imposed scan order. Existing deterministic scans follow space-filling principles but remain fixed and content-agnostic, and can yield fragmented or semantically inconsistent contexts under degradations. We propose \textbf{CoScan}, a \textbf{co}ntent-adaptive \textbf{scan}-order design for causal vision SSMs. CoScan learns image-dependent space-filling traversals via differentiable proxy supervision driven by \textbf{scan-quality objectives} that \textit{encourage short-range coherence and causal predictability, while preserving spatial adjacency}. To support hierarchical restoration backbones, we introduce an \textbf{efficient multi-scale scan construction by coarsening a fine-level minimum spanning tree}, producing coherent scans across feature resolutions. In addition, a \textbf{frequency-guided start selection strategy} is designed to \textit{place informative structures early in the sequence prefix to strengthen causal context formation}. Plugged into existing Mamba-based backbones, CoScan yields consistent improvements across several restoration benchmarks with minimal overhead and shows promising results on high-level vision tasks. Code will be released at https://github.com/dongw22/CoScan

title: CONCORD-Rec: Catalog-Conditioned Modality Utility for Semantic-ID Diffusion Recommendation
authors: Haopeng Jin, Bingkang Shi, Tao Yu, Yifei Ma, Hao Liu, Hongzhu Yi, Jinwen Luo
publish: arXiv
abstract: Multimodal generative recommendation with discrete semantic identifiers (SIDs) requires distinguishing historical modalities that merely alter token predictions from those that genuinely reduce catalog-level ambiguity. When audiovisual, visual, or textual streams are missing, degraded, or semantically conflicting, uniform fusion and unconstrained token gates can propagate misleading content across iterative denoising steps. We propose CONCORD-Rec, a reliability-conditioned discrete diffusion recommender supervised by counterfactual catalog-partition utility. Given a fixed tokenizer and a partially masked SID state, CONCORD-Rec evaluates out-of-fold teacher coalitions over the exact feasible catalog support and aggregates item posteriors across the target code partition at each unresolved position. Rather than distilling raw token probabilities directly, the resulting counterfactual loss differences supervise an availability-masked tokenwise gate that allocates bounded modality residuals around a behavioral denoiser while retaining an exact behavioral fallback slot. We establish theoretical fixed-support ranking stability bounds under gate perturbations and evaluate position-level and code-conditional allocation across audiovisual and image-text recommendation benchmarks under controlled missingness, signal degradation, and semantic conflict. Across 20 source-compatible protocol-dataset rows, CONCORD-Rec improves NDCG by 4%; under matched 30% conflict it improves NDCG by 14.63%. The full-vs-uniform-T=16 sweep improves quality by 2.00-3.58% while reducing p95 latency by up to 86.89%.

title: Rational Ensemble Logic for Cohort Discovery with Real-World Electrophysiology Data
authors: Guo-Qiang Zhang, Xubing Hao, Yan Huang, Xiaojin Li, Licong Cui
publish: arXiv
abstract: Biomedical knowledge representation should make the passage from observations to conclusions transparent, rigorous, understandable, explainable, and reproducible (TRUER). We introduce Rational Ensemble Logic (QEL) for specifying temporal phenotypes in real-world electrophysiology data (RWED), with a meaning independent of the implementation software. QEL combines three parameterized modal operators (exact displacement, bounded existence, and bounded universality) over rational time with Boolean connectives and first-order quantification. Its Labeled Interval Ensemble (LINE) semantics represents annotated records as finite interval ensembles. We relate the operators to morphological operations and develop endpoint-array algorithms and finite rational evidence sets for model checking. We prove closure and semantic correctness of the interval operations, obtain finite evidence sets by quantifier elimination, and establish polynomial data complexity for fixed formulas. On 54 manually constructed records, a prototype agreed with the assigned outcomes for base and strict post-ictal generalized EEG suppression (PGES) queries. A separate feasibility experiment over 1,976 patients identified 37 qualifying patients and 45 annotation patterns in 16 seconds. The released prototype uses endpoint candidates and numerical tolerances. QEL supports the TRUER principle through explicit phenotype definitions, precise semantics, and provably correct evaluation procedures, with rational witnesses for existential queries. These provide a logical foundation for formal specification and correctness of algorithms that are independent of specific clinical interpretation, data annotation quality, and software implementation.

title: Data Poisoning Attacks to Locally Differentially Private Triangle Counting Protocols
authors: Tingxuan Han, Wei Tong, Zijian Wang, Sheng Zhong
publish: arXiv
abstract: Local differential privacy (LDP) has become a crucial paradigm for privacy-preserving graph analytics, enabling graph analytics tasks such as subgraph counting without requiring a trusted curator. However, while LDP provides strong privacy guarantees, the integrity and robustness of LDP subgraph counting protocols in the presence of malicious participants remain poorly understood. In particular, since data are randomized locally before collection, it is inherently difficult to distinguish malicious users from honest ones based solely on their submitted reports, and small, protocol-compliant local manipulations can be systematically amplified through reconstruction and calibration into large global estimation bias. In this paper, we use LDP triangle counting as a representative task to characterize the vulnerability of LDP subgraph counting to data poisoning attacks. For both non-interactive and interactive LDP triangle counting protocols, we analyze their attack surfaces and develop a unified gain-driven framework that captures how adversarial users can manipulate calibrated subgraph count estimates, which we instantiate on representative protocols of both types. Extensive experiments on four real-world graph datasets demonstrate that these attacks can significantly distort triangle count estimates across different protocols and adversarial settings. Moreover, we show that existing and straightforward defenses are insufficient to mitigate these attacks, underscoring the need for robustness mechanisms tailored to LDP subgraph counting.

title: Stars and gas in the most metal-poor galaxies -- II. Search for VMS and determination of stellar population and nebular properties at $Z\lesssim0.1\,Z_\odot$
authors: Aida Wofford, Oskar Aranguré, Christophe Morisset, Calum Hawcroft, Claus Leitherer, Svea Hernández, Gustavo Bruzual, Stephane Charlot
publish: arXiv
abstract: Constraining the properties of OB-star populations and ionized gas at low metallicity is essential for understanding a broad range of astrophysical objects, from stellar black holes to the first galaxies. Rest-frame UV spectra of nearby metal-poor galaxies provide crucial constraints on theoretical predictions of low-metallicity stars and gas. However, such spectra are scarce at $Z\lesssim0.1Z\,\odot$, and candidate Very Massive Stars (VMS) remain elusive. We analyse optical and new UV spectra of nearby star-forming galaxies with $Z\lesssim0.1Z\,\odot$, selected for their nebular He II $\lambda4686$ emission and lack of Wolf-Rayet blue and red bumps, making them promising targets for VMS searches. Some galaxies exhibit stellar wind features (group 1), while others do not (group 2). For group 1, we compare STARBURST99, GALAXEV, and BPASS predictions with observed stellar lines to constrain OB-population ages and masses. The inferred ages are too old for VMS to be present. We also use pySTARBURST99 and GALAXEV photoionization models to investigate the ionized gas in a subsample, finding no evidence for VMS-dominated ionization. The absence of detected VMS may reflect their rarity, our limited sample size, or shortcomings in current models. Moreover, reproducing the extreme optical and UV line ratios simultaneously requires unrealistic N/O, ionization parameters, or Lyman continuum escape fractions, suggesting that multiple ionizing-source populations may be needed.

title: JEV vs. LLMs: A Comparative Analysis for Phishing Email Detection
authors: Muhammad Mahir Malik, Muhammad Moiz Khalid, Hussain Ahmad, Faheem Ullah
publish: arXiv
abstract: Phishing remains a major source of credential theft and fraudulent payments, and email security systems must classify large message volumes reliably, quickly, and at manageable cost. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer flexible text understanding, but their token-based generation increases response time and API cost, and the reliability of their confidence values requires measurement. Jev 1.13, a typed decision model from TypeSafe AI, instead returns a structured outcome with a confidence value. This paper compares Jev 1.13 with Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, and Meta Llama 4 Maverick on a labelled dataset of 1500 emails, covering classification performance, decision latency, token consumption, API cost, and probability calibration. Jev achieves the highest accuracy (79.67%), precision (71.43%), recall (97.97%), and F1 score (82.62%). It also records the shortest batch time (173.88 seconds), the lowest token count (597,895), the lowest cost (USD 0.015103 per 1000 decisions), and the lowest Brier score (0.1698) and ECE (0.1594). These results suggest that Jev is a promising option for fast, structured, high-volume triage. LLMs retain the advantage of generating explanations, which we do not evaluate, and all four systems require further validation before standalone deployment.

title: Axion: A differentiable, GPU-native finite element framework,demonstrated on phase-field fracture
authors: Wei Wang, Meenu Krishnan U., Somdatta Goswami
publish: arXiv
abstract: We introduce Axion (Autodifferentiable, XLA-compiled, Implicit, On-device Numerics), a differentiable, GPU-native finite element framework written in JAX. The element kernels, Newton and Krylov iterations, bound-constrained updates, staggered coupling of fields, and the loop over load increments are expressed as a single program that is just-in-time compiled and executed on the GPU without host intervention. Consistent tangent operators are obtained by forward-mode automatic differentiation of the element residual, and derivatives of the discrete solution with respect to model parameters are obtained by differentiating the same program. Global operators are applied element by element without assembling a sparse matrix, octree mesh refinement is performed within fixed-size arrays, and a cell-based domain decomposition runs the same program on several GPUs. Phase-field fracture is implemented as the first module because it combines fine mesh resolution, bound-constrained damage, and repeated nonlinear solves over a loading history, which together make it computationally expensive. On two- and three-dimensional single-edge-notched tension benchmarks, a uniformly refined Axion computation completes faster than the corresponding adaptive FEniCSx computation. At identical discretization, the two-dimensional benchmark runs 37.9 times faster on one GPU than a FEniCSx implementation on one CPU. Strong and weak scaling efficiencies on four GPUs are 92% and 96%, respectively. Large-scale demonstrations include hydraulic fracture in a poroelastic medium (0.38M degrees of freedom), fracture of a multi-material premolar under contact loading (0.69M degrees of freedom), and a concrete gravity dam (96M degrees of freedom) on a single GPU. The implementation is available as open-source software.

title: Geography of Klein bottle Luttinger surgery
authors: Xinle Dai, Boxi Hao, Shengzhen Ning
publish: arXiv
abstract: We propose and study a modification of Auroux's uniqueness question on Luttinger surgery by replacing Lagrangian tori with Klein bottles. In Kodaira dimension $-\infty$, we introduce two simple graphs whose connected components give bounds and, in several cases, exact counts of Klein bottle Luttinger equivalence classes. In Kodaira dimension zero, we provide examples of numerical invariants supporting infinitely many equivalence classes and prove a homological non-triviality theorem for Lagrangian Klein bottles in all symplectic Calabi--Yau surfaces with positive Euler characteristic. In positive Kodaira dimensions, we construct examples in which Klein bottle Luttinger surgery changes the symplectic Kodaira dimension.

title: The Kazdan-Warner equation on a finite graph with a Neumann boundary condition
authors: Wenyuan Ma, Anfeng Yuan
publish: arXiv
abstract: We study the Kazdan-Warner equation $Δu = c - h \mathrm{e}^u$ on a finite connected domain $Ω$ of a locally finite graph, with Neumann boundary data $\partial u / \partialν= g$. We reduce the boundary condition to homogeneous form and use variational methods and upper and lower solutions to study solvability. Let $c_g \mathrel{:=} |Ω|^{-1}\int_{\partialΩ} g\, \mathrm{d}μ$, and let $ψ$ solve $Δψ= c_g$ with boundary data $\partialψ/ \partialν= g$ and zero mean on $Ω$. When $c = c_g$ and $h \not\equiv 0$, a solution exists if and only if $h$ changes sign and $\int_Ωh \mathrm{e}^ψ\, \mathrm{d}μ< 0$. When $c > c_g$, a solution exists if and only if $h$ is positive somewhere in $Ω$. When $c < c_g$, solvability requires $\int_Ωh \mathrm{e}^ψ\, \mathrm{d}μ< 0$. Under this condition there is a threshold $-\infty \le c_-(h) < c_g$ such that a solution exists for $c_-(h) < c < c_g$ and no solution exists for $c < c_-(h)$. If $h \le 0$ and $h \not\equiv 0$, a solution exists for every $c < c_g$.

title: Evaluating Governed LLM-Driven ML Experimentation: Lifecycle, Provenance, and Failure Metrics
authors: Dowling Wong
publish: arXiv
abstract: Autonomous agents that run ML experiments are usually judged by the best score they reach. That score says nothing about how it was reached: whether the agent stayed within the files it was allowed to edit, whether failed trials were kept or silently dropped, and whether each keep or discard decision can be traced to its evidence. We propose evaluating such systems on their experimental process as well as their outcome, and we build a governed harness that makes this possible. A control plane, not the LLM that proposes changes, owns each trial's lifecycle, checks its edit scope, decides keep or discard, and appends one record per trial to an append-only ledger. Governance metrics such as the invalid-action rate, the repeated-bad rate and provenance completeness are computed from that ledger. Across six ML tasks, from synthetic logistic regression to language-model training, and 1,445 trials, the same contract applied unchanged. The ledger exposed failures that a task score hides: a no-memory arm in which all 120 trials failed, a benchmark adapter whose bounded proposals ran out, and a reset failure that reproducibility hashes revealed, after which the affected campaigns were rerun. In a matched counterfactual, a loop that logs only successful trials left no record of 43 of 50 trials, while the governed ledger recorded all 50. Memory ablations show that memory's effect on repeated bad proposals depends on the task. We release the ledgers of all 1,445 trials, so that every number reported for them can be recomputed.

title: CratesBump: A Version-Bump Dataset for the Rust Ecosystem
authors: Muhammad Hassnain
publish: arXiv
abstract: We release CratesBump, the first public dataset for predicting version bumps in the Rust ecosystem, together with semver-extract, the tool that builds it. CratesBump is built from every crate on crates.io with at least two releases before 14 September 2026 (about 220,000 crates), giving over two million consecutive release pairs. Each pair has 41 features (code changes from AST diffs, dependency changes, complexity, release cadence, GitHub commit and issue activity), its source repository where listed, and two labels: the literal reading of MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, and Cargo's rule, under which a 0.y bump is a breaking change. semver-extract regenerates the dataset from public crates.io data and the GitHub API. To illustrate its use we (i) benchmark bump predictors on held-out repositories, finding the task learnable but far from solved, with lower scores on later releases; (ii) measure which feature groups carry the signal; (iii) check, against declared dependency ranges, how often Cargo's rule shields dependents from pre-1.0 breaking releases; and (iv) audit a sample of releases with cargo-semver-checks, finding minor and patch releases that break the public API despite their version number. Dataset and tool are released under open licenses.

title: LightSEAD: Lightweight SE(3)-Aware Keypoint Detector through Selective Knowledge Distillation
authors: Mayowa Adebambo, Alexander D. Rast, Andrew Bradley
publish: arXiv
abstract: The pursuit of improved performance in deep learning has often been accompanied by increasing architectural complexity and computational demands. We explore an alternative direction: achieving more with less through structured supervision. We introduce LightSEAD, a lightweight SE(3)-aware keypoint detector initialised with calibrated Harris pseudo-labels and enriched through viewpoint-aware and appearance-aware supervision and selective knowledge distillation. LightSEAD comprises only six convolutional layers and 84,289 learnable parameters, achieving competitive repeatability across HPatches, KITTI 06 and 4Seasons while demonstrating its downstream applicability to relative pose estimation on MegaDepth-1500. Further optimised for mixed-precision inference, LightSEAD Coarse achieves approximately 909 FPS on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 and 139 FPS on a Jetson Orin Nano Super.

title: Radar-Native Control Barrier Functions: Doppler Range Rate as a Measured Barrier Derivative
authors: Johannes Mootz, Hesam Mojtahedi, Reza Akhavian
publish: arXiv
abstract: Safe control around dynamic obstacles requires information about both distance and relative motion. Range-based filters commonly reconstruct the required range rate from successive range measurements or from obstacle-state estimators, which can introduce estimator delay or sensitivity to range noise when obstacle motion changes. A frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar measures radial relative velocity directly through Doppler. We use this measurement as the derivative of an ego-centered range control barrier function (CBF) and obtain a closed-form filter on the robot's forward velocity. A measurement margin constructed from sensor error bounds accounts for errors in range, Doppler, ego velocity, and bearing. In 508 paired encounters within the platform's retreat capability, direct Doppler produces two buffer incursions, compared with 15 for a constant-acceleration and 25 for a constant-velocity Kalman filter. On a Unitree Go1, the controller stops at $0.777 \pm 0.015$ m against the predicted $0.758$ m and reacts to a farther approaching object while a nearer static return remains. The guarantee covers the longitudinal range channel under bounded measurement errors and continuously available detections. Direct Doppler removes the need to reconstruct range rate in the safety loop, reducing the delay between a change in obstacle motion and its effect on the safety command.

title: Parisi Energy before Parisi Geometry in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
authors: Maxime Dupont, Bhuvanesh Sundar
publish: arXiv
abstract: The fractured low-energy landscape of spin glasses presents a notorious barrier to optimization. While high-depth calculations indicate that the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can approach the Parisi ground-state energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass, how it does so remains elusive. Here, we treat the QAOA distribution as a statistical-physics object and probe its geometry directly in the thermodynamic limit. We draw two independent bitstrings from the same problem instance and couple them through their macroscopic similarity. We find that typical QAOA samples remain macroscopically uncorrelated, even as their sensitivity to this coupling grows with circuit depth $p$. By contrast, the low-energy tail shows a much stronger tendency to overlap and reveals a Parisi-like phase with the same critical behavior as the thermal spin-glass transition. The onset of this organization moves toward the typical output as the circuit deepens, consistent with the separation vanishing only as $p\to\infty$. Together, these findings suggest a route distinct from structure-exploiting classical algorithms and thermal sampling, one in which the QAOA approaches the Parisi energy before Parisi geometry becomes typical.

title: Polymorph: Operating System Kernel Optimization Through Artificial Intelligence
authors: Dean Sysman, Georgios Liargkovas, Tal Zussman, Hasan Zengin, Petra Hedesiu, Hubertus Franke, Tamar Eilam, Kostis Kaffes, Asaf Cidon
publish: arXiv
abstract: While popular operating systems such as Linux and Windows were originally designed as monolithic kernels, an increasing number of kernel subsystems have become extensible using eBPF. Users can now define custom policies for essential kernel mechanisms, such as the process scheduler, page cache, and network stack, without recompiling the kernel. These mechanisms give developers significant freedom to fit the kernel to their applications' workloads, but the question of which policy to deploy remains open. We study how to use agentic AI to automate kernel policy development, selection, and deployment, focusing on the page cache and the process scheduler as two representative subsystems. We show that existing approaches fall short: evolutionary and agentic search runs offline, is relatively expensive, and often fails to generalize to online workloads, while online knob tuners are encumbered by the knobs' lack of expressivity. In contrast, we propose Polymorph, which learns online: an AI agent writes a generalized, granular policy once, and a user mode tuner adjusts its parameters during runtime, with no LLM in the loop. For the page cache, Polymorph improves throughput over Linux's LRU by 8.4% on unseen data, nearly twice the gain of the best existing policy, while adapting to workload changes at runtime and costing only 16M tokens once, versus 125-240M tokens per workload for agentic offline search. For the process scheduler, it improves on Linux's default by 2.75x across six workloads, versus 2.27x for the best fixed sched_ext policy.

title: MAIC-2 v2.3: A Fortran program for simulating the surface temperature, atmospheric water transport and surface glaciation of the planet Mars
authors: Ralf Greve, Björn Grieger, Oliver J. Stenzel
publish: arXiv
abstract: The Mars Atmosphere-Ice Coupler MAIC-2 is a computationally efficient, zonally-averaged model designed to simulate Martian surface temperature, atmospheric water transport and surface glaciation over timescales of 10^5 to 10^7 years. While sophisticated General Circulation Models (GCMs) provide high-resolution simulations of the Martian atmosphere, their high computational cost makes them largely unsuitable for studies covering millions of years of orbital evolution. MAIC-2 addresses this gap by utilizing physically-based, zonally-averaged parameterizations, including a Local Insolation Temperature (LIT) scheme and a mass balance engine driven by free-convection and instantaneous mixing physics. Version 2.3 introduces a fully modularized Fortran architecture that improves maintainability and ensures that the software remains entirely self-contained, requiring no external numerical libraries or specialized data formats for execution. Demonstrated through a 20-million-year transient simulation, the model successfully reproduces the primary characteristics of the Martian polar layered deposits. MAIC-2 provides the planetary science community with a versatile, open-source tool for investigating the long-term climatic impacts of orbital variations on the Martian surface.

title: Searching the Pareto Front: Multi-Objective Retrieval for Heterogeneous Scientific Modalities
authors: Song Young Oh, Nesar Ramachandra, Bin Xia, Ian Foster, Kyle Chard
publish: arXiv
abstract: In cosmology, surveys span different sky regions and wavelength ranges, resulting in uneven modality coverage across observational datasets. Such heterogeneity can be addressed through either multimodal foundation models (FMs), which learn shared embedding spaces, or independently learned modality embeddings combined via late fusion. We investigate whether the latter provides an adaptive alternative to FM-based scientific retrieval. We evaluate this approach on a galaxy retrieval task spanning diverse modalities--history of star formation, spectra of light emitted, and multi-wavelength observations from two telescopes--comparing an FM baseline with separately trained embeddings fused through multi-objective optimization based on Pareto optimality. We find that the FM baseline achieves strong embedding-space proximity, but our method preserves modality-specific distance structure that allows scientists to inspect which physical signals drive similarity. Our method also achieves improved fidelity in raw-data space: across six measured properties, its nearest neighbor is 8% closer to the query on average than that retrieved by kNN in the FM embedding space (spread 0.128 vs. 0.139). These results suggest that multi-objective retrieval can surface astrophysically coherent candidates that single-objective search alone may overlook.

title: Optimal universal sets for submodular functions
authors: Marek Adamczyk, Richard Ueltzen, Jan Vondrak
publish: arXiv
abstract: We resolve the question of deterministic non-adaptive algorithms for nonnegative submodular maximization: We prove that for every $n \geq 2$ and $ε\in (0,\frac{1}{4})$, there is a polynomial-size family ${F}_{n,ε}$, $|{F}_{n,ε}| = n^{O(1/ε^2 \log (1/ε))}$, such that for every nonnegative submodular function $f:2^{[n]} \to {\bf R}$, $\max_{S \in {F}_{n,ε}} f(S) \geq (1/4 - ε) \max_{S \subseteq [n]} f(S)$. It is also easy to show that a factor better than $1/4$ cannot be achieved by any fixed polynomial-size family. A related result that we prove is that there is a distribution ${D}_{n,ε}$ supported on polynomially many subsets of $[n]$ such that $(1 - ε) {\bf E}_{R \sim {U}_n}[f(R)] \leq {\bf E}_{R \sim {D}_{n,ε}}[f(R)] \leq {\bf E}_{R \sim {U}_n}[f(R)]$, where ${U}_n$ is the uniform distribution on $2^{[n]}$, and $f$ is any nonnegative submodular function. This is interesting in light of the fact that uniform convergence does not hold for submodular functions: Sampling polynomially many sets from ${U}_n$ and taking the empirical mean does not converge to the true expectation uniformly for all submodular functions. The construction of ${F}_{n,ε}$ and ${D}_{n,ε}$ is based on a new semidefinite extension of submodular functions: We show that the Goemans-Williamson rounding technique for a near-orthogonal arrangement of vectors gives a value close to the uniform expectation, and this rounding can be derandomized, since near-orthogonal vectors can be constructed in logarithmic dimension.

title: Smoothing and Learning for Movement-Robust RSS-Based Spoofing Detection
authors: Usama Mir
publish: arXiv
abstract: Physical-layer spoofing detection identifies an attacker who impersonates a legitimate wireless user by checking whether transmissions claiming the same identity originate from different locations, using the received signal strength (RSS) measured at several receivers. A recent scheme by Romero et al. makes this approach robust to user movement by combining a neural-network position-change detector (PCD) with community detection on a graph of frames and a fixed threshold on a hand-crafted test statistic. I study two modifications to this scheme. First, I smooth the sequence of PCD scores with a median or Gaussian temporal filter before thresholding. Second, I replace the fixed decision threshold with a supervised classifier operating on six statistical features of the region sequence produced by community detection. On real indoor RSS measurements from 52 transmitter locations, Gaussian filtering raises PCD accuracy from 0.870 to 0.921 when the PCD is trained on 10 locations and from 0.905 to 0.925 when trained on 40. On synthetic attack and no-attack sequences built from the same measurements, evaluated on a held-out test set of 1,679 sequences, the best classifier (XGBoost) reaches an accuracy of 0.949 and an F1 score of 0.940, and random forests reach an AUC of 0.99. The detector separates static attackers almost perfectly but misses about a third of attacks in which two transmitters move simultaneously, which produce region sequences similar to those of a single moving user.

title: Zippers and Twisters II: The lopsidedness of satellite systems around local massive galaxies emerges from a shifting cosmic web landscape
authors: Janvi P. Madhani, Charlotte Welker, Sneha Nair, Katarina Kraljic, Christophe Pichon, Yohan Dubois
publish: arXiv
abstract: We investigate the role of the cosmic web on the origin and strength of lopsidedness in the distributions of luminous dwarf satellites around massive galaxies analogs in the high-resolution hydrodynamic simulation NewHorizon. Using common lopsidedness estimators, we find that $>25\%$ of our sample display ``statistically significant" lopsidedness incompatible with expectations for dark matter sub-haloes. The NewHorizon sample is generally skewed towards being more lopsided than naive expectations. This cautions against using dark matter or under-resolved hydrodynamic simulations as a null-hypothesis to compare to real systems. We find broad, hemispheric lopsidedness to be much more prevalent than narrow lopsidedness inherited from group infall. Across all systems, the dividing plane between the richest and emptiest hemispheres is systematically aligned with a nearby intermediate-scale cosmic filament. Further analysis reveals that the lopsidedness of systems is largely inherited from that of the network of filaments feeding them. The most populated side almost systematically contains the highest number of filaments. Such anisotropies of local filament networks are often indicative of on-going or recent zippers (filament merger $<2$ Gyr). Converging filamentary structures therefore funnel satellites preferentially onto one side of host halos, naturally generating lopsided configurations without requiring galaxy mergers. Twister remnants (of high orbital momentum mergers of filaments) are also found on the richest hemisphere of our systems, perhaps reminiscent of vorticity preventing mergers hence causing satellites' pooling. These results suggest that lopsidedness is primarily an outcome of the evolution of the intermediate-scale cosmic web. This highlights the need for increased hydrodynamic resolution in simulations.

title: Capability Internet: A Network Architecture for Autonomous Agents
authors: Zhuoming Wen, Hongwei Li, You Wu
publish: arXiv
abstract: Autonomous agents increasingly provide and consume network services. An agent coordinating a long-running task across organizations must track what has been done, which actions are authorized, and which provider can perform the next step. We propose Capability Internet (CI), an architecture in which agents exchange capabilities and coordinate their use through persistent tasks. Versioned descriptions specify behavior, and live instances identify the providers and resources that can supply it. Task records link each invocation to its selected instance, authority, and terms of use. When providers change, the task can reuse completed results that still meet its requirements. Five functions support capability discovery, task coordination, federated compute, intelligence reuse, and governance of capability use and settlement. Reviewed task results can supply versioned intelligence for subsequent tasks. We illustrate CI through four deployment profiles covering computing and intelligence services, manufacturing, vehicles and embodied robots, and space-ground operations, and propose an evaluation plan.

title: Plug-and-Play Multi-Licensee Robust Watermarking for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
authors: Jianshuo Liu, Kang G. Shin, Haining Wang
publish: arXiv
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures enable high-capacity large language models (LLMs) with high sparse computation, making them attractive for deployment on private hardware. However, distributing model weights exposes valuable intellectual property (IP) to leakage and unauthorized redistribution, creating an urgent need to both verify model ownership and trace leaked copies to individual licensees. Existing model-watermarking techniques are ill-suited for meeting this need because they are fragile under MoE's dynamic routing or require costly retraining to embed a distinct watermark for each licensee, thus making scalable distribution difficult. To address these challenges, we present PPMoE, the first plug-and-play multi-licensee watermarking framework for MoE LLMs. Rather than training a separate model per user, PPMoE trains a compact set of mergeable incremental weight modules that steer the MoE router toward distinct, mutually compatible routing patterns. During model distribution, the model owner selectively merges unique combinations of these pre-trained, mutually compatible modules into the base model on the fly, embedding a licensee-specific watermark without additional training. PPMoE supports reliable multi-licensee attribution under both white- and black-box threat models. In the white-box setting, attribution is done by inspecting triggered routing decisions or the merged weight modules responsible for these decisions, whereas in the black-box setting, attribution relies on analyzing output token likelihood ratios. Extensive experiments across five state-of-the-art MoE models, seven benchmark datasets, and varying number of licensees show that PPMoE achieves very high attribution accuracy while preserving base model utility and maintaining strong robustness to various adaptive watermark-removal attacks.

title: Symplectic $\mathbb{CP}^n$ recognition and filling rigidity via Rabinowitz Floer homology
authors: Zhengyi Zhou
publish: arXiv
abstract: We prove that a symplectic manifold $X$ admitting a pseudo-holomorphic line through two generic points, formulated as the non-vanishing of a genus zero Gromov--Witten invariant, is (rationally) homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb{CP}^n$, with identical first Chern class and quantum cohomology. Together with generalizations of this result to pseudo-holomorphic lines with tangency constraints, they provide a new mechanism for establishing the topological uniqueness of Liouville fillings of certain contact manifolds. We obtain filling rigidity for the ideal boundary of a class of affine varieties that admit $\mathbb{CP}^n$ as a compactification; notable examples include the ideal boundary of the complement of any hyperplane arrangement and $ST^*\mathbb{RP}^n$ for $n\ge 3$. The proofs are based on Rabinowitz Floer homology and its variants.

title: Covering the Pauli Observables: Sampling Thresholds and the Design Effect of a Measurement Setting
authors: Kausthubh Chandramouli, Noah Siekierski, Bojko N. Bakalov, Dror Baron
publish: arXiv
abstract: Quantum state tomography and shadow-based estimation rely on measuring Pauli observables. An experiment does not measure them one at a time: it chooses a measurement setting that assigns one of the bases X, Y or Z to each qubit, and a single run in that setting yields estimates of every Pauli observable compatible with it. We say that the setting covers those observables. We determine how many random settings cover a prescribed fraction of all Pauli observables. As the number of settings grows exponentially with the number of qubits, the covered fraction has a sharp threshold at a growth rate of $3^{3/4}$ per qubit, set by the rate-distortion function of covering at zero distortion. We give an explicit expression for the number of settings needed to reach a target fraction, accurate up to a remainder that reduces to a small oscillation for many qubits, and show that random sampling is asymptotically optimal up to a factor of less than 1.69. Coverage does not determine what a setting contributes to an estimator. Observables covered by one setting are estimated from the same outcomes, so their estimates are correlated. We quantify this correlation through the design effect of a setting, which equals the squared Pauli expectation that the setting captures and depends on the target state. We derive its mean over settings in closed form for every state and show that it can be estimated without bias from the measurement data. In simulations on six qubits, measuring settings needs 7.6 to 38 times fewer circuit runs than measuring the same number of observables independently. At high coverage, fitting the outcome histograms instead of averaged estimates roughly halves the reconstruction error, mainly because the fit counts how many settings cover each observable. The correlation itself costs such a fit about a factor of two, and a larger design effect signals more to gain from modeling it.

title: Observation of Exact Mobility-Edge Phases in Two-Dimensional Photonic Quasicrystals
authors: Chaohua Wu, Yingying Shi, Juan Kang, Qinglong Zhang, Shuo Liu, Gang Chen
publish: arXiv
abstract: Mobility edges, separating localized and extended states in energy, are central to localization physics. While exact mobility edges have been established in several one-dimensional quasiperiodic models, their realization in two dimensions remains largely unexplored. Here, we uncover a general route to exact mobility edges in the two-dimensional Aubry-Andre quasicrystal by introducing auxiliary subsystems. Through isospectral reduction, we reveal a hidden self-dual structure that yields exact mobility-edge conditions, separating extended, localized, and partially localized states in the spectrum. Tailoring the auxiliary structures controls the effective couplings and resulting mobility edge configurations, while auxiliary resonances further support flat-band states. In a decorated Lieb-type quasicrystal, we experimentally realize these predicted phases in photonic waveguide lattices and probe their energy-dependent localization through site-selective quench dynamics. Our results provide a versatile platform for controlling localization and can be readily extended to other physical platforms and higher-dimensional systems.

title: Chromatic heights of homotopy fixed points of iterated topological Hochschild homology of connective spectra
authors: Jiaxi Zha
publish: arXiv
abstract: Let $R$ be an $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectrum of height $m$. The chromatic redshift theorem implies that its $n$-fold iterated algebraic $K$-theory $K^{(n)}(R)$ has height $m+n$. Moreover, there is a natural map $K^{(n)}(R)\to (T^n\otimes R)^{hT^n}$, where $T^n\otimes R$ denotes the $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology. Hence it is natural to ask whether the target also has height $m+n$. Although this fails in general, we prove that it holds whenever $R$ is connective and $m\geq1$. Our proof is based on an iterative calculation using Wilson spaces and relative topological Hochschild homology. As an application, we determine the support of the $T^n$-homotopy fixed points of $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology of $\mathrm{BP}\langle m\rangle$ for $n=2,3$ with $\mathrm{BP}\langle m\rangle$ equipped with any $\mathbb{E}_3$-$\mathrm{MU}$-form.

title: NEXONN: Advancing the NEXOTRANS Exoplanet Atmospheric Retrieval Framework with Transformer-Based Neural Posterior Estimation for JWST Transmission Spectroscopy of WASP-39b
authors: Tasneem Basra Khan, Liton Majumdar, Mithun Patra, Tonmoy Deka, Swastik Dewan, Priyankush Ghosh, Vishal Meena
publish: arXiv
abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope is delivering unprecedented constraints on exoplanet atmospheres, but computationally intensive Bayesian retrievals challenge the transition from individual planets to population-level studies of planetary formation and evolution. We introduce NEXONN, a transformer-conditioned normalizing-flow framework within NEXOTRANS that enables rapid atmospheric posterior estimation with uncertainty quantification. Incorporating PandExo-based JWST noise, we benchmark NEXONN against PyMultiNest using simulated spectra and JWST observations of WASP-39 b (0.6-12 microns). For simulated MIRI/LRS data, eight posteriors achieve a mean overlap of 80.32%. Retrievals of combined NIRISS, NIRSpec, and MIRI observations yield consistent atmospheric properties. For the full dataset, NEXONN infers C/O = 0.82 (+0.01/-0.02) and [M/H] = 1.13 (+0.04/-0.04), compared with PyMultiNest values of 0.80 (+0.03/-0.01) and 1.19 (+0.05/-0.03). Divergence metrics, Wasserstein distances, posterior overlaps, and coverage tests assess posterior fidelity and uncertainty calibration, revealing parameter-dependent differences. Once trained, NEXONN performs posterior inference within seconds, enabling scalable population studies of exoplanet atmospheric composition, formation, and evolution.

title: Breaking the Myth of Four-Tier Stacked Transistors for Logic: an Investigation from Process to Device and Block-Level PPA
authors: Jianxiang Jin, Haoran Lu, Yihan Luo, Yanbang Chu, Yibo Zhang, Jingru Jiang, Yuji Cheng, Wanyue Peng, Xun Jiang, Feiyu Teng, Kairang Guo, Ming Li, Yibo Lin, Runsheng Wang, Heng Wu, Ru Huang
publish: arXiv
abstract: For the first time, this work evaluated whether 4-tier stacked transistors can translate the straightforward density gains into realistic chip-level scaling benefits. A practical dual-sided 4-tier transistor-stacking CFFET (Flipped CFET-to-CFET) process was proposed, on which a DTCO framework spanning standard-cell design, local interconnects, RO analysis, and physical implementation was built under 2A node design rules. The CFFET was also benchmarked with its 2-tier transistor-stacking counterparts FFET. Among CFFET configurations, the best-performing Symmetric Power still lags FFET by 11.2% in RO frequency due to the complex MOL parasitics. At the block level, CFFET reduces the Ibex RISC-V core area by only 12.8% (far below the 40% nominal cell-height reduction), while running 10.9% slower at iso-power. We further introduced a novel Tetris-like cell stitching to minimize the area overhead, which allows non-rectangular cell design and recovers 7.4% area in a 1-bit ALU design. An optimized NanoStack CFFET was finally proposed, inspired by previous work. This work indicates that straightforward vertical 4-tier stacking proves insufficient to guarantee enough PPA benefits, though the resulting design insights may guide future advanced architectures.

title: SFiD: Self-Supervised Fitness-Driven Optimization for Next-Generation Networking
authors: Kalpesh K. Patel, Ekant Sharma, Sandeep Kumar Singh, Lajos Hanzo
publish: arXiv
abstract: Next-generation (NG) wireless networks face increasingly complex and dynamic optimization challenges driven by data-intensive applications and massive device connectivity. Existing methods suffer from one or more limitations, including high computational complexity, poor scalability and adaptability, reliance on large labeled datasets, or weak generalization in dynamic and non-convex wireless environments. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a self-supervised fitness-driven diffusion (SFiD) method that autonomously generates its own training data and iteratively learns from it. It also exhibits strong generalization capabilities and the ability to effectively tackle challenging optimization problems. We validate the convergence of our proposed method to the global optimum on both analytical convex and non-convex optimization problems. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, we consider reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) phaseshift optimization in cell-free massive multiple-input multipleoutput (CF-mMIMO) systems with imperfect channel state information and spatial correlation at the RIS as a case study. Specifically, we develop SFiD-C for continuous variable optimization and apply it to optimize continuous RIS phase shifts in CF-mMIMO systems. We also develop SFiD-D for discrete variable optimization and apply it to optimize discrete RIS phase shifts in CF-mMIMO systems. Furthermore, we develop a binary neural network (BNN) based version of SFiDD for reducing its computational complexity, referred to as SFiD-D (BNN). Finally, our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed methods markedly improve computational efficiency and achieve comparable or superior performance compared to meta-heuristic and DRL benchmarks for both continuous and discrete RIS phase-shift optimization.

title: Validating Concurrent Correctness Witnesses with Ghosts by Thread-Modular Abstract Interpretation
authors: Michael Schwarz, Zhendong Ang, Umang Mathur
publish: arXiv
abstract: Concurrent programs are notoriously difficult to write and to reason about, and even tools based on sound theoretical foundations can produce incorrect results due to implementation bugs. Correctness witnesses have been proposed as a way to increase the confidence in the verdicts of software verifiers by enabling independent validation. Recently, correctness witnesses have been extended to the concurrent setting, by introducing ghost variables to allow encoding more expressive invariants. While different approaches to producing witnesses with ghosts exist, validation techniques are still lacking; instead of leveraging the information encoded in the ghosts to guide the validation process, validators merely treat ghost instrumentation and invariants over ghost variables as additional proof obligations. We propose a novel framework for the validation of concurrent correctness witnesses that exploits the semantic information encoded in ghost variables. It combines a checking phase, which establishes the semantic content of the ghost instrumentation, with an exploitation phase making use of this information. Both phases are formulated as thread-modular abstract interpretation. In particular, we consider two different classes of ghost variables and techniques for exploiting them, one based on resource invariants and one based on phases. Phase ghosts guide the degree to which the abstract interpretation considers interleavings instead of always abstracting them coarsely. In this way, the abstract interpreter can validate witnesses containing invariants beyond the reach of unguided thread-modular analysis, while still retaining its scalability benefits. We have implemented our framework in a static analyzer and evaluate it on witnesses encoding resource invariants obtained from a state-of-the-art software verifier, as well as on hand-crafted witnesses encoding phase information.

title: Finite-time stochastic resetting in bounded domains: competing targets, energetic cost, and optimal search strategies
authors: Hanshuang Chen, Chongyao Tang, Guofeng Li
publish: arXiv
abstract: We investigate the first-passage dynamics and energetic cost of a Brownian particle subject to finite-time stochastic resetting in a bounded one-dimensional domain with two absorbing boundaries. Unlike conventional instantaneous resetting, the particle is returned to a prescribed resetting position through a finite-duration process driven by a linear trapping potential. By solving the corresponding backward equations, we derive analytical expressions for the mean global first-passage time and the splitting probabilities. Our results show that the finite duration of the return process can substantially modify the dependence of the mean global first-passage time on the resetting rate. In particular, we identify a critical trapping strength above which resetting can accelerate the search process, and characterize how the range of favorable resetting positions depends on the trapping strength. We further characterize the energetic cost of resetting by deriving the generating function of the total work and obtaining an analytical expression for its mean value. For the linear trapping potential considered here, we establish an exact relation between the mean total work and the mean cumulative return time. This relation allows us to establish a quantitative trade-off between the mean global first-passage time and the energetic expenditure, revealing how the finite duration of the return process affects search efficiency. Brownian dynamics simulations confirm our theoretical predictions.

title: Interface Weyl electrons in the kagome-bilayers
authors: Keiki Ishida, Kohei Fujiwara, Shun Sasano, Kazuki Nakazawa, Takeshi Seki, Seigo Souma, Daisuke Shiga, Hiroshi Kumigashira, Takafumi Sato, Ryo Ishikawa, Naoya Shibata, Yukitoshi Motome, Atsushi Tsukazaki
publish: arXiv
abstract: What makes a topological character prominent is whether its characteristic electronic states are located near the Fermi energy. While the kagome-metals possess unique topological characteristics owing to their distinctive electronic band structures, i.e. flat and Dirac bands, the control of Fermi energy to accentuate these characteristics has scarcely been studied in these materials. Here, we propose a new concept for activating the topological characteristics of Weyl electrons specifically near the interface of kagome-bilayers, namely interface Weyl electrons. The kagome-bilayers prepared by a sputtering technique surprisingly exhibit atomically abrupt interfaces thanks to the suppression of interdiffusion for maintaining the crystal symmetry of the hexagonal-type D0$_{19}$ and cubic-type L1$_{2}$ structures. Much higher electrical conductivity of the kagome-bilayers compared to single-layer films indicates the emergent contribution of a highly conductive electronic state at the interfaces. The enhanced electrical conductivity and the exceptionally large anomalous Hall conductivity about 2000 $Ω$$^{-1}$cm$^{-1}$ in the intrinsic mechanism indicates that the emergent interface electronic states comprise Weyl nodes in the D0$_{19}$ structure identified in our theoretical band calculations, triggered by nontrivial charge transfer. These results demonstrate that topological transport can be engineered at the interface of intermetallic compounds, leading further design principles towards development of device functionality.

title: Subsystem evolution in the history state formalism
authors: A. Boette, F. Lomoc, N. Canosa, R. Rossignoli
publish: arXiv
abstract: We present a relational framework for characterizing the evolution of quantum composite systems, based on the correlations within a history state describing the whole evolution relative to a quantum reference clock. While total system-clock entanglement entropy consistently measures the unitary evolution of the closed global system, a different picture emerges for the reduced state of an open subsystem, whose evolution is generally non-unitary due to environmental coupling. We introduce a general formalism that quantifies open-subsystem dynamics using a subsystem-clock mutual information derived from the history state. We demonstrate that this quantity serves as a consistent quantifier of subsystem evolution with respect to a given clock basis, can be applied to arbitrary dynamics, and reduces to system-time entanglement entropy in the global limit. Furthermore, maximizing this measure over all clock bases yields a basis-independent bound on the maximum evolution achievable relative to the clock, directly linked to the difference between the subsystem's entanglement with the rest of the history state and its entanglement with the environment. Finally, we derive analytical expressions for qubit clocks, illustrate our results using spin 1/2 and spin 1 quantum walks, and present a full matrix formalism of Kraus operators for describing the most general subsystem evolution.

title: STORM: A Lightweight Structure-Free Model for Binding Affinity Prediction
authors: Ayush Pandit, Rohan V. Koodli, Wei Deng, Roxana Daneshjou, Ron O. Dror
publish: arXiv
abstract: Accurately predicting a small molecule's binding affinity to a protein, a critical task in drug discovery, remains challenging. Physics-based approaches like free-energy perturbation (FEP) have very high computational costs and require expert setup. Recent machine learning--based cofolding models have reported accuracy approaching that of FEP---and at least one of them, Boltz-2, has already been widely adopted for affinity prediction---but they remain expensive for large computational screens and even more expensive for retraining on newly collected experimental data. To address these challenges, we introduce STORM: Similarity Transfer from Observed Reference Molecules. STORM is a fast, simple machine learning model that ensembles many small model fusions of diverse protein and molecule representations for binding affinity prediction. Trained on the same data, STORM matches or exceeds the accuracy of Boltz-2 on multiple evaluation datasets, while delivering a speed improvement of over five orders of magnitude for both inference and training. Our results also suggest opportunities to substantially improve affinity prediction accuracy by integrating historical experimental affinity data with structural and biophysical information.

title: Anytime-valid goodness-of-fit test by $e$-spacings
authors: Yunda Hao, Kin Wai Chan
publish: arXiv
abstract: To perform an anytime-valid goodness-of-fit test, we propose spacing-based \(e\)-processes that control the type-I error rate under arbitrary stopping rules. Based on the maximum spacing of order statistics, we construct spacing-based \(e\)-processes for nonparametrically testing distribution. The resulting procedures are simple and computationally efficient, and are power-consistent. We call them $e$-spacing tests. This approach is especially powerful in detecting localized discrepancy between the data-generating density and the null density. Under mild conditions, the logarithm of the proposed \(e\)-process is asymptotically equivalent to that of the oracle-optimal \(e\)-process. We further generalize the construction from maximal spacing to maximum spacing set in the form of the \(1/k\) fraction of the largest \(m\)th order spacings, as a measure of the lower-level set of density. It boosts power under more global discrepancy from the null. Furthermore, we propose a greedy predictable scheme, via argmax or softmax rules, to combine multiple $e$-spacing testing strategies. We prove that it optimally tunes the $e$-spacing test. The proposed approach is readily generalizable to multivariate testing via a coordinate-wise Rosenblatt-transform. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed methods perform favorably relative to the considered anytime-valid competitors as well as various types of multiple test-adjusted Kolmogorov--Smirnov tests.

title: Improve How You Improve: Recursive Policy Self-Improvement for Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Multi-Object Navigation
authors: Yang Li, Ziju Han, Aming WU, Zihao Zhang, Sijia Zhang, Yahong Han, Qinghua Hu
publish: arXiv
abstract: To advance the development of embodied general navigation, zero-shot open-vocabulary multi-object navigation has attracted increasing attention, aiming to enable robots to efficiently search multiple objects in unseen environments without training. For this task, the key lies in improving navigation policies from earlier searches to locate subsequent goals more efficiently. Recent methods automate this process through trajectory reflection and rule revision, enabling policy self-improvement. However, the mechanisms for diagnosing problems and generating revisions are typically designed by humans and remain fixed across iterations. Consequently, the system's capacity for continued self-improvement remains constrained, even as its navigation policy evolves. To this end, we propose RPSI-Nav, a Recursive Policy Self-Improvement framework for zero-shot multi-object navigation that revises both the navigation program and its revision mechanism. RPSI-Nav diagnoses search behavior, requests diagnostic views when existing observations cannot distinguish competing causes, and generates targeted navigation revisions. Feedback from subsequent goal searches is linked to the rules that produced these revisions, guiding changes to diagnosis, observation acquisition, and revision planning. The updated improver governs subsequent navigation improvements, forming a recursive loop in which RPSI-Nav revises its own improvement process. Across goals, the robot conditionally inherits accepted program updates and spatial memory, enabling search experience to improve both future navigation and adaptation. Benchmark experiments and qualitative real-robot evaluations validate RPSI-Nav's effectiveness.

title: Mitigating the Grid Impact of Gigawatt-Scale AI Data Centers via High-Fidelity Model Flexibility
authors: Eihab E. E. Ahmed, Saeed Manshadi
publish: arXiv
abstract: Gigawatt-scale artificial intelligence data centers (AIDCs) are being connected at a single point of interconnection (POI) faster than transmission can be reinforced, yet studies of their flexibility rely on DC power flow and simplified load envelopes that omit voltage, cooling dynamics, and workload deadlines. This paper addresses this gap by embedding a high-fidelity AIDC model, with separate inference and training pools, hall thermal mass, PV, a battery energy storage system (BESS) with reactive capability, and a STATCOM, in a five-minute multi-period AC optimal power flow. Simulations on the RTS-GMLC test system show that active-power flexibility mitigates local price spikes and relieves congestion, whereas reactive support from the BESS inverter or a STATCOM is needed to keep the POI voltage away from sagging around its 0.95~pu limit. Sensitivity analyses show that cost-driven charging of large batteries can induce new morning congestion and that storage largely substitutes for wider workload deferral.

title: On primes not adjacent to $2$ in the prime graphs of almost simple groups
authors: Maria A. Grechkoseeva, Anatoly S. Kondrat'ev, Nanying Yang
publish: arXiv
abstract: The prime graph $GK(G)$ of a finite group $G$ is the graph whose vertices are primes dividing the order of $G$ and in which two distinct primes $r$ and $s$ are adjacent if and only if $G$ has an element of order $rs$. The $2$-independence number of $GK(G)$ is the maximal size of independent vertex subsets in $GK(G)$ containing the vertex~$2$. We determine all almost simple groups whose prime graph has a vertex $r$ not adjacent to $2$ and find the $2$-independence numbers of all almost simple groups.

title: Mean Curvature Minimizing Foliations Of A Vector Field
authors: Tabish A. Syed, Marc Theveneau, Benedikt Wirth, Rustum Choksi, Kaleem Siddiqi
publish: arXiv
abstract: Streamline patterns are ubiquitous in nature. Prominent examples include white matter fibre tracts in the mammalian brain and arrangements of elongated cells, such as cardiomyocytes in the heart wall. It has been posited that such organisations foliate into locally smooth surfaces to optimise function. However, the recovery of these foliations from a single vector field aligned with the local orientation of the underlying sheets remains an open problem. We address this challenge by introducing a mathematical model of a sheet and developing an algorithm for sheet inference, from measurements of the oriented structures. Given an input vector field, our model estimates a second vector field that is orthonormal to it, while also requiring the Lie bracket of the two to vanish. To balance sheet likelihood against low surface area, we also reduce the mean curvature of the recovered local surface. We compute the first variation of an associated energy and provide a numerical method which admits an efficient, parallel implementation for sheet estimation. We demonstrate our approach on both synthetic and biological examples, motivated by applications to medical imaging. These include white matter fibre tracts from a brain atlas and confocal microscopy images of cleared heart wall tissue. For the latter we are able to reconstruct sheets aligned with local cardiomyocyte directions at unprecedented (micrometre) scale.

title: Authenticating IoT Data on Ethereum after Pectra and Fusaka: A Cost Study of Signature Schemes, Batching and Anchoring for Agricultural Supply Chain Finance
authors: Ming-Fong Sie, Jian-Hong Chen, Gwan-yen Lin, Yen-Shuo Chen, Shih-wei Liao
publish: arXiv
abstract: Blockchain-based supply chain finance can turn the sensor-recorded production history of smallholder farms into verifiable credit evidence, but only if every record is authenticated and anchored at a cost that scales to large device fleets. Ethereum's 2025 Pectra and Fusaka upgrades changed this cost landscape: they added precompiles for BLS12-381 and P-256, repriced calldata and MODEXP, and capped transaction gas at $2^{24}$. We organize the authentication and anchoring of IoT records into three trust levels, from posting a Merkle root through a trusted aggregator to verifying every device signature on-chain, and implement four replay-protected signature designs: ECDSA over secp256k1 and P-256, BLS aggregate signatures with on-chain hash-to-curve, and a pseudonymous identity-based signature with batch verification. Measured as signed transactions under the rules before and after both upgrades, the upgrades mainly changed which designs are feasible, not their cost. Batching and Merkle anchoring cut the cost of ECDSA authentication sixfold, to 8,963 gas per record, and secp256k1 ECDSA remains the cheapest authenticated design: P-256 costs 1.6 times as much, the identity-based design 2.7 times and BLS aggregation 3.9 times, dominated by on-chain hashing to the curve. One transaction carries at most 1,754 ECDSA-authenticated records but only 411 BLS-aggregated ones. On a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, pairing-based signing takes 5.7 ms against 0.29 ms for ECDSA. Pairing-based designs pay off only when the application needs their additional properties, and the identity-based design adds key escrow at the key generation centre. The benchmark harness is released for reproducibility.

title: Geiss-Besov Regularity of Exit Times of Diffusion Processes
authors: Yao Chen, Jiagang Ren, Hua Zhang
publish: arXiv
abstract: We prove that the truncated exit times of possibly degenerate diffusion processes from open domains satisfying the exterior sphere condition belong to the Geiss-Besov space $\mathbb{B}_p^{\frac{1}{2p}}$. In the one-dimensional case, the same result is proven using Zvonkin transformation for untruncated exit times if the diffusion is uniformly elliptic.

title: Charged Schrödinger blocks in $1+1$ dimensions from the quartic Casimir and endpoint equations
authors: Hirohiko Shimada
publish: arXiv
abstract: We construct charge-two Schrödinger conformal blocks in one spatial dimension, independently of any dynamical realization. We consider ordered vacuum four-point functions of fundamental fields of dimension $1/2$, with homogeneous Schrödinger equations at the earliest and latest insertions and interactions allowed in the intermediate two-particle interval. For reduced blocks analytic in signed spatial coordinates and even under simultaneous spatial inversion, two functions of the time cross-ratio determine the full spatial dependence: the collinear value and a rescaled mixed spatial derivative. An exact Kummer lift, built from confluent hypergeometric functions, gives this reconstruction. An operator identity reduces the quartic Casimir equation, modulo the endpoint equations, to an equivalent coupled system for this pair. At generic exchanged dimension, OPE conditions select a unique block up to normalization for each primary parity. We obtain collinear ${}_4F_3$ functions and sums of Kummer products, including the shadow branches. The blocks depend on the relative sign of the signed coordinates, distinguishing piecewise linear worldlines with an inflection from those with monotone segment velocities. In the Calogero model, we recover the previously derived bosonic four-point function and obtain its fermionic counterpart, with an independent integral check. At the diffusion-limited fixed point of $A+B\to\emptyset$, two blocks of opposite primary parity give the same collinear unlike-species response. Nonnegativity for all positions and ordered times selects the even family, thereby establishing that the response summed over species contains the even shadow pair with dimensions $Δ=1,2$. The nonnegativity argument demonstrates a concrete constraint for a Schrödinger bootstrap beyond collinear data.

title: GramStatTexNet: Efficient, Interpretable, and Neuro-Inspired Texture Analysis-by-Synthesis
authors: Vasha DuTell, Zuyu Yun, Anne Harrington, Michael Y-S Fang, Mark Hamilton, Christian Kövesdi, Edward H. Adelson, William T. Freeman, Ruth Rosenholtz
publish: arXiv
abstract: Deep networks achieve high realism in texture synthesis but often rely on opaque, over-parameterized representations that have limited direct connection to biological vision. Neuroscience-informed pyramid models are interpretable, compact, and biologically inspired, but rely on small, hand-curated statistics sets that are difficult to generalize or extend. We introduce GramStatTexNet, a hybrid analysis-by-synthesis framework that combines the multi-scale Gabor filter structure of classical models with the flexibility of Gramian-based correlations, organized into structured filter families. This structured representation enables analyses that are challenging for deep-feature methods: each statistic carries a named filter-family identity, allowing us to decompose synthesis fidelity into per-family contributions and to learn an interpretable, low-dimensional embedding that preserves perceptual texture content. We compare our framework to classical and deep texture-synthesis baselines across diverse texture categories, and on multiple perceptual metrics, highlighting the compactness and interpretability advantages of this hybrid representation, alongside competitive synthesis quality. This same framework extends naturally to peripheral textures via spatial pooling, and to dynamic textures using a spatiotemporal filter bank. GramStatTexNet provides a unified, interpretable framework for analyzing and modeling visual information with natural extensions across space, time, and eccentricity. Project page: https://vdutell.github.io/gstn

title: Modeling LLM Reasoning Dynamics with Structural Representations
authors: Ilia Karpov, Andrey Atamanyuk, Dmitry Ilvovsky, Aleksandr Anokhin, Alex Elizov, Dmitry Zagorulkin, Sergei O. Kuznetsov
publish: arXiv
abstract: Language-model reasoning alternates between sustained activities and local operations. We study how this temporal structure predicts continuation and the computation needed to analyze it. T/E/S combines text, local events, and spans of activity. Across reasoning and information-seeking tasks, events and spans improve next-outcome prediction in 70 of 76 evaluation groups for a Transformer and 74 of 76 for Qwen with LoRA. Span duration and preceding events are associated with transitions, and retaining event history across span boundaries improves prediction. We formulate budget-allocation counting and action-conditional continuation queries, prove counting hardness under explicit encodings, and derive conditions for affordable decision certification. In finite-process experiments, bounds that cancel shared continuation mass recover the same optimal actions as full dynamic programming while reducing mean inference CPU time by 77.7%. On 71 held-out HotpotQA and MuSiQue questions, a compact structural observer improves prediction of whether a fixed inference procedure finishes within a CPU allowance: Brier loss falls from 0.0836 to 0.0756. An annotation audit identifies substantial errors in that observer, separating this computational result from semantic validation of its features.

title: Strongly Suppressed Cosmic-Ray Diffusion in a Wind-Blown Cavity Environment of SNR G21.8-3.0
authors: Yuan Li, Gwenael Giacinti, Yang Su, Xiao Zhang, Hui Li, Yang Chen
publish: arXiv
abstract: We report the discovery of a GeV $γ$-ray source spatially offset from SNR G21.8-3.0, while no significant high-energy emission is detected from the remnant itself. Using 16 yr of \emph{Fermi}-LAT observations together with $^{12}$CO ($J=1-0$) data, we show that the GeV emission is spatially associated with a localized molecular cloud located just outside a gas cavity whose boundary closely follows the SNR shell. This configuration supports a scenario in which cosmic rays (CRs) escaping from the remnant propagate through a progenitor-carved low-density cavity and illuminate nearby dense gas. Modeling of the cloud emission requires a diffusion coefficient suppressed by a factor of several tens relative to the canonical Galactic value, indicating strongly inhibited CR transport around the remnant. Rather than serving as a simple low-density escape channel, the wind-blown cavity appears to regulate CR propagation through local magnetic structure and enhanced turbulence. This system therefore provides evidence that circumstellar structures can control the escape and early transport of CRs around supernova remnants.

title: The Geometry of Mode Sampling in Reconfigurable MIMO Channel Extrapolation
authors: Shaoyang Sun, Chongwen Huang
publish: arXiv
abstract: Pattern-reconfigurable arrays acquire channels by distributing radiation modes across their antenna elements. Equal mode counts fix the observation budget while leaving a spatial sampling choice that directly affects reconstruction of unmeasured channels. We establish how this assignment enters the inverse problem through the receive aperture and the coupling between propagation paths. For an isolated path with calibrated positive real responses, the power-weighted variance of antenna positions completely characterizes the assignment dependence of the profiled angle information at fixed mode counts. We then construct layouts with identical weighted apertures and different path correlations, exposing a limitation of aperture-based design in multipath propagation. A paired simulation study evaluates balanced random, contiguous, interleaved, and equal-moment sampling using a common estimator with per-detection joint angle refinement. Balanced random sampling substantially reduces complete-channel error relative to ascending contiguous blocks when some modes are entirely unobserved, with improvements across nearly all tested scenes at high signal-to-noise ratio. When every mode is sampled, the mean benefit is more sensitive to rare large errors. Together, the analysis and experiments connect the spatial distribution of mode measurements to both extrapolation accuracy and reconstruction stability.

title: Toward Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Neural AC Power Flow
authors: Ojas Sanghi, Anvita Bhagavathula, Alvaro Carbonero, Priya L. Donti
publish: arXiv
abstract: Growing uncertainty in power system operations from renewables integration, extreme weather, and data center loads challenges the reliability of traditional power flow solvers at scale. Machine learning-based proxies are a potentially promising alternative, but the prohibitive cost of generating training data for large grids makes out-of-distribution generalization a key capability for deployment; currently, models trained on small grids lack that capability. In this work, we systematically evaluate how physics-informed losses, multi-grid training, and perturbation-based data augmentation improve the zero-shot transfer of three graph neural network-based power flow models from smaller systems to a larger, unseen 500-bus system. We find that (1) physics-informed losses improve transfer relative to purely supervised objectives; (2) multi-grid training on smaller systems matches the best single grid but does not close the gap to target-grid training; (3) perturbation-based augmentation on edge attributes improves transfer by up to 54.6%; and (4) random line/generator dropout does not consistently improve performance.

title: AdaS-ViT: Test-Time Adaptive Routing for Spiking Vision Transformers with Ultra-High Energy Efficiency
authors: Zecheng Hao, Zihan Huang, Shenghao Xie, Jiyuan Zhang, Zhaofei Yu, Tiejun Huang
publish: arXiv
